column1: # Operator direction (2026-10-06, opencharly/.github#170): the auto-close bound is ONE
# count-based number again — AI_REVIEW_AUTO_CLOSE_AFTER (org default 5) — over the
# validator's `BLOCK` verdicts PLUS its engine/EVAL `INCONCLUSIVE` verdicts. A verdict-less
# run that is a CLEAR INFRASTRUCTURE failure (the provider endpoint or the GitHub runner —
# not the engine) is EXCLUDED from the count: it must never close a PR on its own. The
# INFRA/EVAL split is the `Verdict class: infra` line the INCONCLUSIVE notice emits, which
# the counter matches by the EXACT literal. AI_REVIEW_AUTO_CLOSE_AFTER=0 switches the bound
# off entirely. This REVERTS the #169 per-class split (ONE INCONCLUSIVE closed immediately).
# The close notice must carry the remedy, not just the fact: a fresh branch and a fresh
# thread, with every finding already fixed (the operator's instruction verbatim), AND state
# that clear infra failures did not count toward the bound.

column5: open a clean (pull request|PR) from scratch

column1: # charly#796: the org's ONE required context is `validate / validate`, so a repo's own `ci`
# was enforced by NOBODY and a head with a red `go` could merge (measured twice: charly#795,
# charly#791). The fix moved that enforcement INSIDE the required check — two deterministic
# gates — so the rulebook must stop claiming branch protection covers it, and the workflow
# `filter=latest` is the DEFECT, not the fix: during a re-run GitHub drops the check name
# from it entirely (measured), so a gate reading it arms auto-merge on a head whose check is
# mid-re-run. The URL fragment, not the bare word — the file names `latest` in prose to
# explain why it is not used.

column5: BRANCH PROTECTION DOES NOT ENFORCE IT
enforced by that first gate, NOT by branch

column1: # SAME-REPO vs EXTERNAL-FORK (opencharly/.github dsh-github#2, 2026-10-07). The org-required
# caller must gate the validate job on `head.repo.full_name == github.repository` — the
# head repo is a DIFFERENT repository than the base — NOT on `head.repo.fork == false`,
# which is TRUE for every PR in a first-party FORK repo (opencharly vendors several upstreams
# as forks: dsh-github, crabbox, the pi-* family). The retired predicate skipped the org's OWN
# same-repo PRs, so the ruleset's REQUIRED `validate / validate` was never produced and the PR
# could never merge. The new form skips ONLY a genuine external contribution.
# The forbid pattern targets the ACTIVE form — an `if:` line using the retired predicate —
# not the prose that explains why it is retired (the same technique as the
# `check-runs...filter=latest` row above: the file names the retired form in a comment, so a
# bare-substring forbid would fail on its own explanation).
# opencharly/opencharly#446 — R1 "fix it or file it" replaces the thematic-batch deferral: a
# blocking finding is fixed in the change, a non-blocking one is FILED and listed under the PR
# body's `## Filed issues`. Stated in the rulebook, the strict-policy source, the validator
# rulebook, and the PR template; the retired batch-as-deferral wording may survive in none.

column5: R1 — RCA every anomaly, then fix it or file it
